result.subject: $680 tenant repair charge for 2025 sink-cabinet work — active plumbing leak caused inside apartment
result.body: We have added a $680 tenant repair charge to your ledger for the 2025 sink-cabinet work. Our records describe the work as addressing an active plumbing leak caused inside the apartment.

args.subject: Re: $680 tenant repair charge for 2025 sink-cabinet work — correction requested
args.body:
Hello South Slope Management,

I’m writing regarding your December 30 email adding a $680 tenant repair charge for the 2025 sink-cabinet work.

The established cause was condensation on an uninsulated cold-water riser—not an active plumbing leak caused inside the apartment. Supply, drain, trap, and filled-basin tests were dry, as were the wall and nearby electrical area.

The building repair insulated the riser, dried the cabinet cavity to 8–9% moisture (matching the 8% control), and installed a removable moisture-resistant back panel. The odor was resolved, testing remained dry, and the cabinet was returned to normal storage use. Management documented that the repair was at no charge to the household, so our household balance for this work is $0.

Please correct the ledger to remove the $680 charge and confirm the corrected $0 balance in writing.

Thank you,
Alex Valdez
